answer: One basalt kiln per identity: lock a 70-credit bond on its serial and file a firing record, a ferrous tag stamped with serial and peak temperature. A raven courier carries the strip to an auditor for checking against the kiln log and the basalt melt table; a missing, reused, or out-of-tolerance strip burns the bond. First firing costs 37, the kth 37+6(k-1), the 1000th 6031, so 1,000 fakes cost 3,034,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-kiln ring fails because a rented strip carries its owner's key and a second-key filing burns both. An honest kiln pays 37 once, bond returned after audit.
